page: Amazon Web Services m8gn.12xlarge is a general-purpose, network and EBS-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores utilizing the ARM64 architecture with an AWS Graviton ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 2.8 GHz. The processor provides 64 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 36 MB L3 cache per core, with no multi-threading. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware.

Benchmark results indicate strong multi-core capabilities and top-tier memory performance. The server achieved a top-tier rating in multi-core Geekbench testing (24039.0) and software compilation (71201.0), alongside strong multi-core stress-ng performance (81868.98). Memory bandwidth is a notable strength, with top-tier results in large-block read (435.08 GB/sec) and write (216.67 GB/sec) operations, as well as a top-tier PassMark memory score. Database operations and static web serving throughput also reached top-tier levels, with static web serving at 98.12 GB/sec. However, single-core performance is more moderate, with average ratings in stress-ng single-core CPU tests and PassMark CPU scores.

The lack of local storage means all storage operations must rely on network-attached EBS volumes, though this is mitigated by a baseline network bandwidth of 150 Gbps. For workloads, the instance is efficient for memory-bandwidth-intensive tasks, database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded processing. While it demonstrates strong text generation performance for medium and large LLM models, its text generation speed for small models is rated as poor, indicating a potential bottleneck for specific lightweight inference tasks. The ARM64 architecture offers high resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded enterprise applications, web serving, and database management.

It features 192.0 GB of RAM (4.0 GB per core), 150 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU. However, single-core performance and small-model LLM text generation are relatively weaker. This server is qualitatively cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads, offering high resource density for database management, software compilation, static web serving, and network-intensive enterprise applications.
